Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the UniBank Financial Corp Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Johnson, Investor Relations Director. Please go ahead.

Sarah Johnson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review UniBank Financial Corp's results for the Q3 2024. With me this morning are Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer; David Kim, Chief Credit Officer; Emily Vargas, Chief Technology Officer; and Robert Hayes, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to Johnathan Reyes.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. UniBank Financial Corp delivered exceptional results in the Q3 2024, exceeding expectations and demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Accelerating revenue growth
2. Improving profitability
3. Managing risk effectively
4. Investing in technology and innovation
5. Enhancing customer experience
6. Strengthening our brand
7. Delivering value to our shareholders.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on key areas starting with our provision for credit losses, including drivers and methodology. In Q3, our provision for credit losses came in at $285 million, an increase from $210 million in Q2 and $195 million in the prior-year period. This equates to a provision rate of 45 basis points on average loans, up from 35 basis points last quarter. Our total allowance for credit losses stands at $4.2 billion at quarter-end, or 1.28% of total loans held for investment—a solid coverage level compared to the peer average of 1.15%, according to S&P Global data.

Our approach follows the CECL standard, implemented like peers such as JPMorgan Chase and Bank of America since 2020, estimating lifetime expected losses from day one across our $325 billion loan portfolio. We combine quantitative models with qualitative adjustments, using Probability of Default (PD), Loss Given Default (LGD), and Exposure at Default (EAD) based on over 20 years of historical loss data and internal migration matrices.

PD modeling employs logistic regression and survival analysis on more than 15 million obligor records, broken down by segments like commercial & industrial (C&I), commercial real estate (CRE), residential mortgages, consumer installment, credit cards, and auto loans. LGD includes downturn adjustments—42% for unsecured C&I and 25% for collateralized CRE—drawn from workout data and discounted cash flows. EAD accounts for prepayments and draws on commitments, adding a 10% utilization factor for revolvers.

Macro overlays are central, with 12 scenarios from Moody's generator weighted at 40% base, 35% adverse, and 25% severe. Inputs feature GDP growth at 1.8% for 2024 (revised down from 2.2%), unemployment at 4.1%, office vacancies at 18.2% nationally per CBRE, and Fed funds peaking at 5.25-5.50% with three 25 basis point cuts in the first half of 2025. We've upgraded with an XGBoost machine learning ensemble on our AWS risk platform, boosting PD accuracy by 15% over legacy models, confirmed through backtesting on 2023 regional bank events.

This quarter's provision stemmed from portfolio shifts, credit migration, and macro factors. Commercial real estate headwinds accounted for 55% of the increase, with our $85 billion CRE portfolio—40% office, 30% multifamily, 20% retail, 10% industrial—requiring a $120 million build. Office delinquencies over 30 days rose to 1.2% from 0.9% quarter-over-quarter, echoing national trends with over 20% vacancies in NYC and San Francisco due to remote work. We added 10 basis points reserve on office amid cap rate pressures and equity risks, though multifamily steadied with LGD at 22% on Sunbelt rent growth in Texas and Florida. We've de-risked by syndicating $2.5 billion in office loans year-to-date and limiting underwriting to 65% LTV.

Consumer segments showed resilience but auto pressures for 25% of the uplift, with $45 billion in consumer loans driving $70 million provision. Credit card delinquencies stayed at 2.8%, below the 3.1% FDIC industry figure, supported by our rewards-focused Visa portfolio like Capital One's. Auto delinquencies on $12 billion subprime indirect climbed to 1.1%, up 40 basis points, linked to high used-car prices at Manheim Index 105 and 8%+ rates; net charge-offs annualized at 3.2%. We've cut subprime dealer originations to under 15%.

C&I and wholesale made up 20%, with $120 billion portfolio contributing $65 million as PD rose to 1.8% in tech and manufacturing from inventory issues. Firm-wide net charge-offs were $180 million or 58 basis points annualized, stable quarter-over-quarter, with 45% recoveries, strong in SBA 7(a) and EIDL. Qualitative overlays added $30 million for geopolitical issues like Middle East energy credits and Florida mortgage climate risks.

Regionally, Northeast and Mid-Atlantic (35% of portfolio) saw 60 basis points reserve growth from CRE office in Boston and Philly; Southeast/Sunbelt (25%) balanced multifamily gains against auto in Atlanta/Charlotte; West Coast (15%) felt tech layoffs on C&I but stable venture debt; international (10% via London/Toronto) flat on hedged CAD CRE.

Trends show firm-wide delinquencies at 1.05%, down 5 basis points, early-stage 30-59 days at 0.65%, criticized assets 2.8%, non-accrual 0.75%—better than Wells Fargo's 0.95%. Charge-offs below two-year averages. Our Risk 360 initiative with AI early warnings caught 20% more deteriorations, enabling $500 million restructurings. We've grown investment-grade munis 15% year-over-year and passed DFAST severe with CET1 at 11.2%. For Q4, expect $240-260 million provision (38-42 bps), with releases possible in 2025.

Next, credit quality metrics like NPL ratio, charge-offs, and delinquencies reflect disciplined underwriting amid a resilient economy. Our NPL ratio—90+ days past due or non-accrual excluding government loans—was 1.15% at quarter-end, down 25 basis points from Q2's 1.40% and 65 from last year's 1.80%, our lowest since 2019 and below KBW peer average of 1.45%. A $125 million NPL drop came from CRE and consumer auto resolutions.

Delinquencies improved with 30+ days at 1.95%, down 15 basis points sequentially and 40 year-over-year; 60+ at 0.85%, down 10. Credit card early delinquencies rose slightly to 2.3% from seasonal spending and rate lags but 75 basis points under JPMorgan peers.

Net charge-offs annualized at 0.62%, steady from Q2's 0.61% and down 18 from last year's 0.80%, totaling $185 million. Consumer at 1.85% (cards 3.2%, auto 1.1%), commercial 0.25%, mortgages 0.15%; unsecured personal peaked at 4.1% then stabilized via skip-tracing.

Consumer (45% loans) solidified with auto 30+ at 1.2%, repossessions 0.4% half industry; cards pressured by 22% APRs but ML warnings cut losses $20 million. Commercial (35%) NPLs 0.95% vs. FDIC 1.65%; CRE office (8% total loans) 90+ at 2.1% but watch-lists down 10%; C&I middle-market 0.4% in healthcare/logistics.

Residential (15%) under 1% delinquencies, negligible NCOs, 85% GSE, non-QM 0.8% NPLs no ARM resets till 2025.

Regions: Southeast (55% loans) 0.85% NPLs on low unemployment/housing; Midwest 1.3% with reshoring; Northeast CRE 2.8% office leading to 20% cut in NYC commitments; Mexico 1.1%.

GenAI risk scoring on 70% consumer originations upped accuracy 12%, cut losses 8%; RPA collections up cure 22%. ALLL 2.85x NPLs, 285% NCOs, reserve $2.1 billion up $50 million. Expect NPL trough 1.1% Q4, 1.2-1.3% 2025; NCO 0.55-0.65%. CET1 12.2%.

On operating expenses, trends and drivers: Expenses totaled $2.48 billion, up 7.2% year-over-year from $2.31 billion but flat from Q2's $2.49 billion. At 59.8% of revenue, improved 120 basis points from 61%; adjusted efficiency 58.4% vs. 61.2% last year, beating full-year under 60% target and peer median 62%.

Compensation/benefits $1.12 billion (45%), up 5.1%: 4.2% salary inflation for tech/risk talent, headcount +1.8% to 48,200 in digital/wealth, incentives +8%; offset by 15% Manila/Bangalore offshoring, -3% onshore back-office.

Tech/data $512 million (21%), +14.6%: $250 million AWS/Azure cloud 65% done saving 12% mainframe; $45 million genAI like BankAI Assistant for chatbots/fraud; $120 million cybersecurity zero-trust post-CrowdStrike; APAC +22% for Alipay wallet.

Occupancy/equipment $285 million, +3.8%: 45 branch closures to 2,100, embedded finance with Walmart/Target -2% seq; hybrid hardware up modestly.

Professional/regulatory/marketing $421 million, +9.2%: M&A/litigation up, FDIC down 15%; $180 million compliance Basel IV/ESG SFDR; $95 million marketing +18% digital NA.

Other $162 million, -2%: lower T&E.

Regions: NA (65%) +6% offset by Temenos T24; Europe (20%) +12% UK MiFID III offset Dublin; APAC/EM (15%) +15% HDFC JV/Indonesia.

Outlook: <5% growth FY24, 57% efficiency via 20-25% automation ($150m savings), procurement $80m, 2-3% headcount opt. ROE 11-12%, $1.2b buybacks.

Efficiency ratio progress and targets: Adjusted non-interest expense over total revenue at 58.2%, down 330 basis points from Q2 61.5% and 660 from last year 64.8%, best since pre-pandemic, ahead KBW 60.1%. Revenues $12.4 billion +8% QoQ from NIM/deposit mix, trading/wealth fees.

Segments: Consumer 56.4% digital app 28m users +15% YoY -22% branch costs; Commercial 59.1% AI underwriting -40% time $150m savings; Wealth 60.8% +450 bps automation.

Regions: US 57.0% low 25% deposit betas Texas/Fla like Ally; EMEA 61.5% +500 bps 120 closures DORA/Basel; APAC 54.2% Grab wallet +35% vol -30% CAC.

Cloud 70% $220m savings to $350m; RPA 65% back-office -12% ops headcount; AI cross-sell +18% attachment.

Targets: FY24 57-58%, Q4 57.5%; 2025 52-54% like Goldman via $500m AI fraud BaaS, $400m procurement, 15k branches. Deposit +4.2% CET1 12.1%.

Fee income breakdown for wealth management, investment banking, cards: Non-interest $2.8 billion +18% YoY +5% QoQ, 28% revenue record. Market rally S&P +12%, M&A.

Wealth $1.25b +22% (45%): AUM $1.7t +16%, inflows $45b record 60% HNWIs. Equities/alts +14/11%; ESG Alpha Fund $15b AI $12b inflows like BlackRock; UniAdvisor AI 96% retention +15% cross-sell UniLink API. NA 55%, APAC +35% RMB; EMEA flat UK offset Zurich ME. Alts to 25% AUM KKR JV margins 72%.

IB $850m +15% (30%): Advisory +28% $420m 45 >$1b deals $25b TechCorp $150m #4 cross-border; ECM $18b IPOs HealthAI $4.2b conv $12b +40%; DCM $35b IG spreads -15bps green $10b EU Taxonomy. Quantum Pricing -20% cycles vs Goldman. Americas 60%, EMEA 25% energy, APAC 15% SEA IPOs. FY $3.2-3.5b sponsor/activist.

Cards $700m +12% (25%): Interchange $455m 65% vol $250b +11%; service $245m. Consumer +13% travel +22% Visa Infinite 25m +18%; corp $80b +15% UniBiz SAP/Oracle. Plaid Open BNPL ARPU $120 +8%; tokenization -25% fraud. US +14%, Europe +10% SEPA, LatAm +20% Mexico. 15% CAGR token/crypto vs Stripe/Adyen. Pipeline $15b NPS 95% ROE 22%.

Cost of deposits average rates and competitive pressures: Average cost 2.47% +28 bps QoQ +112 YoY from Fed hikes, peer-aligned KeyCorp/Regions betas 45-50%. Cumulative beta 48%, QTD 52% < super-regionals 55-60%.

NIB 32% mix -35% YoY cost 0.15% +12 bps sticky C&I 98% retention >$10m sweeps. IB 3.12% +42 bps: savings/NOW 42% 2.65% +35 vs Ally/SoFi 4.20-4.50%; MM 3.45% tiered <3.75% bundle; time 14% 4.28% +65 SOFR+10-20 minimal brokered <2%.

Regions: Midwest 2.35% +4.2% core Hometown Rewards; Southeast 2.65% vs BofA/Wells 4%+ inflows $1.2b.

Pricing analytics Q2 dynamic -18% promo +2.8% growth; Deposit Optimizer nCino 12% zero-beta NIM 3.42%; jumbo CDs 4.50-4.75% 65% convert. Q4 +20-25 bps beta 45% +10 bps NIM ROA >1.20%. Deposits $48.2b +3.1% LDR 82%.

Revenue diversification initiatives and impact: Amid rate volatility Fed 5.25-5.50%, geopolitics, fintechs, shifted from 62% NII FY21 to 42% non-interest TTM $48.7b revenue, NII 53%. Non-interest +18% $20.5b +65 bps RO TCE 14.2%.

WAM AUM $1.8t +22% Heritage acq like MS/UBS; fees $4.2b +25% green $12b EU SFDR $3.5b flows margins 45%.

Transaction/payments ApexPay $250b +35% $1.8b +12% Plaid/Adyen FX APAC 15%; NA BNPL Shopify $900m losses 2.8% AI.

CIB IB $2.9b +14% ECM +28% Arm IPO HY $45b structs $650m VaR $25m.

Regions: EMEA 22% +19% Commerz DACH €8b; APAC 18% Singapore UHNW $15b; LatAm Brazil wallet $400m +3x vs US cards 3.2% delinq.

Tech $1.2b AWS lakes NPS 72 +15% wallet; vol std dev 8.2% from 12.5% CET1 12.8%. Target 50/50 split 10-12% fee CAGR 4% expense CIR 58% mid-teens EPS.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, Johnathan, and good morning. UniBank Financial Corp reported net income of $1.2 billion for the Q3 2024, or $2.45 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 12% driven by higher loan balances and improved net interest margin. Non-interest income was up 15%, reflecting strong performance in wealth management and investment banking. Our capital ratios remain strong, and we are well-positioned to support future growth.

Lisa Patel:
Thank you, Michael. From a risk management perspective, we are closely monitoring interest rate risk, commercial real estate exposure, and cybersecurity threats. We are taking proactive steps to mitigate these risks and maintain a strong risk profile.

David Kim:
Good morning. Our credit quality remains exceptionally strong with NPL ratio at 1.15% and net charge-offs at 0.62%. We are actively managing our loan portfolio and remain confident in our ability to navigate the current economic environment. Specifically, the performance of our commercial real estate portfolio has been strong.

Emily Vargas:
Thank you. I'd like to provide an update on our technology initiatives. We are making significant progress on our digital transformation, including the launch of our AI-powered mobile banking app which has seen 30% increase in customer adoption and efficiency gains.

Robert Hayes:
Good morning. We are focused on operational excellence and driving efficiency across the organization. Key initiatives include branch optimization and automation of back-office processes, which are contributing to improved productivity and cost savings.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will open the floor for questions. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide further insights into provision for credit losses?

Johnathan Reyes:
Thanks John. As detailed earlier, the $285 million provision reflects CECL modeling with macro scenarios and segment-specific pressures, particularly CRE office at 55% of the build and auto in consumer. We've enhanced models with XGBoost for better accuracy and de-risked via syndications. Q4 outlook is $240-260 million assuming no recession, positioning us well for ROCE over 10%.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Carter with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Carter:
What are your plans for revenue diversification initiatives?

Michael Chen:
Great question, Emily. We've boosted non-interest to 42% of revenue through WAM growth to $1.8 trillion AUM, payments via ApexPay $250 billion volumes, and CIB fees up 14%. Regional expansion in EMEA and APAC hedges risks, targeting 50/50 NII/fee split by 2025 with 10-12% fee CAGR.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
How are you managing credit quality metrics?

Lisa Patel:
Thanks David. NPLs at 1.15% improved sharply, NCOs stable at 0.62%, delinquencies trending down. GenAI scoring and RPA collections are key, with coverage strong. We see stabilization into 2025 barring recession.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Rachel Wong with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Rachel Wong:
Can you discuss the performance of fee income breakdown?

David Kim:
Absolutely, Rachel. Wealth at $1.25 billion +22% on AUM inflows and ESG; IB $850 million on M&A/ECM; cards $700 million volume-driven. Diversified growth across regions supports 28% revenue mix.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to Johnathan Reyes for any closing remarks.

Johnathan Reyes:
Thank you for your interest in UniBank Financial Corp. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
